📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan will head to Greece on Thursday with the need to overturn a negative trend, so Ruben Amorim will leave nothing to chance.

Industry observers note that in the past few weeks (barring the international break), Milan have alternated good performances at weekends with disastrous midweek results. The collapse against Bologna is one example, while losses to Bournemouth and Ferencvaros have complicated the Europa League mission.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Amorim won’t be opting for the usual excessive rotation against Olympiacos on Thursday night in Athens. There will be some changes, but the coach will field several regular starters.

The paper report that Amorim knows full well that victory is the only acceptable result in order for the Rossoneri to get back on track in their substantial to qualify for at least the Europa League play-offs, with the top eight now a distant mirage.

Recent findings suggest that the Portuguese will rest Luka Modric in midfield. He will be replaced by Ardon Jashari, who scored his first goal for the Rossoneri in the win over Genoa. Adrien Rabiot – the Rossoneri’s driving force in this first part of the season – will remain in the team.

The defensive choices are almost forced, with Koni De Winter and Sankhoun Diawara still the centre-backs. Strahinja Pavlovic is not yet 100% fit and will undergo further tests on the kidney stone challenges that have kept him out for the last month, even though he played 20 minutes on Sunday.

Up front, the same attack that played against Frosinone should be seen, namely Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira supporting Gonçalo Ramos, who finally returned to scoring after more than a month without a goal.

Both Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchison are raring to go, but both are expected to start on the bench in Athens, ready to come on as substitutes. Beyond the players, it will be crucial for Milan to take to the pitch with the right attitude.

Liverpool confirm 22-man squad for Club Brugge as Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch decisions revealed

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 13:08.
  • Liverpool have confirmed their 22-man travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.
  • The Reds are going in search of their fourth win from five continental matches in Belgium, having overcome Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and LASK Linz before a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce last time out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 13:08.

Liverpool have confirmed their 22-man travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

The Reds are going in search of their fourth win from five continental matches in Belgium, having overcome Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and LASK Linz before a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce last time out.

Andoni Iraola's men have responded to that setback with back-to-back Premier League wins, though, following up a 3-1 triumph at Crystal Palace with a 4-0 battering of Manchester United on Sunday.

Teenage starlet Rio Ngumoha stole the show against the Red Devils in the absence of Cody Gakpo, who was an unexpected absentee from Sunday's matchday squad due to a calf injury.

Iraola revealed that Gakpo suffered his injury while on international duty with the Netherlands, and the attacker has not been included in the travelling party for Wednesday's game.

Gakpo's problem is not believed to be serious, though, and there is a chance that he will be fit to return for the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

As well as Gakpo, compatriot Ryan Gravenberch will also miss Liverpool's trip to Brugge, as the midfielder continues his recuperation from a small heel fracture.

After the weekend's win over Man Utd, Iraola expressed hope that Gravenberch would be fit for the Champions League clash, having returned to training while carefully managing his pain.

However, the Netherlands international will now miss a fourth consecutive game for Liverpool, and he is still waiting for his first minutes of November, having also been an unused substitute against Arsenal.

Gravenberch and Gakpo are two of five Liverpool absentees against Club Brugge, as Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley (both knee) have not made the cut either.

The rest of Liverpool's squad is as expected, and alongside Ngumoha, five other Kirkby youngsters could earn opportunities to impress at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Nineteen-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni could make his fourth consecutive start in the Champions League after appearing from the off against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce, scoring against the latter.

Twenty-two-year-old James McConnell is also involved, but the midfielder has been restricted to just one nine-minute cameo in the UCL against Villarreal so far.

Wide man Luke Chambers, meanwhile, was given five minutes off the bench against LASK, but he has not made a single Premier League matchday squad this season.

Finally, attacking duo Lewis Koumas and Jayden Danns could earn valuable European minutes; the latter is yet to make a competitive appearance for Liverpool under Iraola.

  • United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are right now considered the favourites to secure his signature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are right now considered the favourites to secure his signature.

With the teenager’s first-team opportunities limited in Germany, the Premier League champions could look to take advantage of the situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

According to recent reports, the report claims City are prepared to offer the 17-year-old lucrative personal terms as they step up their pursuit. Their interest is serious, with the club previously prepared to meet a valuation in the region of €20 million (£16.7m).

Chelsea are also long-term admirers of the youngster and were reportedly willing to spend a similar amount last winter. Paris Saint-Germain previously made contact with Dortmund in 2025, while Arsenal and Liverpool have more recently been monitoring his situation.

However, City are right now viewed as being in the strongest position should Dortmund soften their stance.

In a recent development, albert joined Borussia Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has rapidly established himself as one of the most exciting young American talents in European football. He has already made Bundesliga appearances and earned senior international recognition with the United States.

It has been revealed that despite his potential, opportunities under Niko Kovac have been limited this season. That lack of regular first-team football has encouraged several clubs to monitor his development, although Dortmund remain determined to keep hold of their young attacker.

The Bundesliga side have reportedly rejected approaches, including loan enquiries, and continue to view Albert as an important part of their long-term plans. They are also preparing a contract extension offer, with his current agreement running until June 2027.

There is another crucial factor for City. Premier League regulations prevent English clubs from signing Albert permanently until he turns 18 in May, meaning any potential transfer would be geared towards next summer rather than an immediate move.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Ferencvaros will be aiming to make it five wins in the league stage of the 2026-27 Europa League when they welcome Celje to Budapest on Thursday night.
  • The Greens will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 loss to Gyor in the league, while Celje recorded a 2-0 victory over Grosuplje in their last domestic game on November 22.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:24.

Ferencvaros will be aiming to make it five wins in the league stage of the 2026-27 Europa League when they welcome Celje to Budapest on Thursday night.

The Greens will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 loss to Gyor in the league, while Celje recorded a 2-0 victory over Grosuplje in their last domestic game on November 22.

Ferencvaros have been excellent in this season's Europa League, beating Celtic, Viktoria Plzen, Torreense and AC Milan in the league stage of the tournament, with 12 points leaving them in third position in the table, level on points with the top two Benfica and Bournemouth.

Balazs Borbely's side were 2-0 winners over Milan in their last European match, which was a statement result, but their six-game winning run in all competitions came to an end on November 21 when they were overcome by Gyor in Hungary's top flight.

Ferencvaros reached the last-16 stage of the 2025-26 Europa League, ultimately losing to Braga, and they have been regulars in the knockout round of the competition of late.

It would be a shock if the Hungarian team were unable to progress to the knockout stage of this season's tournament given their strong position in the table.

Ferencvaros will take on Lech, Juventus and Hoffenheim in their final three games in the league stage of this season's Europa League.

Celje, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's competition, with four points leaving them down in 25th spot in the table.

The Yellow and Blues are opened their campaign with back-to-back losses to Bayer Leverkusen and Omonia before claiming a point in a 2-2 draw with Red Bull Salzburg.

Zoran Zeljkovic's side then recorded a 3-2 victory over Sturm Graz in their last European fixture, and Celje have actually won their last five matches in all competitions.

The Yellow and Blues have not been beaten since the 3-0 reverse to Omonia in the middle of October, so they will enter Thursday's match in strong form.

Celje played in the Conference League last season, reaching the last-16 stage of the tournament before going down 4-2 on aggregate to AEK Athens.

Ferencvaros Europa League form:.

Ferencvaros form (all competitions):.

Ferencvaros will be missing Bence Otvos on Thursday through injury, while Bamidele Yusuf is suspended for the European fixture with Celje.

Kristoffer Zachariassen has been in excellent form this season, scoring 11 goals and registering nine assists in 25 appearances, and the 32-year-old will again be in the side.

Meanwhile, there should also be a spot through the middle for Lenny Joseph, who has six goals and three assists in 18 appearances during the current campaign.

As for Celje, no injuries have been reported ahead of the contest.

Svit Seslar has been the team's standout player this season from an attacking point of view, scoring 11 goals and registering two assists in 24 appearances, and the 24-year-old is set to start.

There is also expected to be a position through the middle for Armandas Kucys, who has netted five times for Celje during the 2026-27 campaign.

Ferencvaros possible starting lineup:.

Dibusz; Osvath, Raemaekers, Gomez, Nagy; Madarasz, Maiga; Zachariassen, Bero, Birmancevic; Joseph.

Celje possible starting lineup:.

Leban; Ivansek, Bejger, Tutyskinas, Avdyli; Zabukovnik; Dukuly, Seslar, Kvesic, Verbic; Kucys.

Celje's form is excellent, but Ferencvaros have been one of the standout teams in the Europa League this season, and we are backing the hosts to shade a close match on Thursday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have earned a reputation for recruiting some of the best young players in world football in recent seasons.

The additions of Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and more recently Jeremy Jacquet and Luca Brughmans are proof of the philosophy in place within Liverpool's recruitment team.

With Julian Ward at the helm, the recruitment strategy doesn't seem to have changed, and the Reds continue to be linked with some of the most promising young talents from across Europe and beyond.

Liverpool's mission remains the same but that doesn't mean that they are automatically the favourites for every wonderkid, and they appear to be falling behind in the race for one highly rated defender.

Liverpool behind in race for next Van DijkRuud Nijstad is quickly becoming one of the most exciting prospects in the Eredivisie, and the Dutch U19 international is earning himself plenty of attention. The 18-year-old has started all but one game for FC Twente in the league this season, and has established himself as a central part of John van den Brom's side. Standing at 6'5, Nijstad already holds the stature of a Premier League defender, and his impressive performances for Twente, both domestically and in the UEFA Conference League, have led to interest from several top sides.

Ruud Nijstad is rapidly becoming one of the most exciting prospects in the Eredivisie, and the Dutch U19 international is earning himself plenty of attention.

The 18-year-old has started all but one game for FC Twente in the league this season, and has established himself as a central part of John van den Brom's side.

Standing at 6'5, Nijstad already holds the stature of a Premier League defender, and his impressive performances for Twente, both domestically and in the UEFA Conference League, have led to interest from several top sides.

A report from Ekrem Konur recently named Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Manchester United as the four clubs with the most advanced interest, and it appears that Liverpool are already falling behind in the race for the next Dutch colossus.

Nijstad is also capable of playing at left-back and is left-footed, making him an ideal long-term replacement for Virgil van Dijk.

Having the chance to learn from the man who captain's his national team could be vital for Nijstad, who could command a fee of over €30 million (~£25m) according to Konur.

Liverpool clearly aren't leading the race for Nijstad, but he would be an excellent January pick up and Ward & Co should definitely be taking a look at the 18-year-old.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.
  • The Spanish right-back has attracted attention following his performances for Spain at the World Cup, but Spurs have several reasons to feel confident about keeping hold of the defender.
  • According to Catalan broadcaster 3Cat, Porro is one of Laporta’s preferred defensive targets as Barcelona consider whether to strengthen their backline in January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.

The Spanish right-back has attracted attention following his performances for Spain at the World Cup, but Spurs have several reasons to feel confident about keeping hold of the defender.

According to Catalan broadcaster 3Cat, Porro is one of Laporta’s preferred defensive targets as Barcelona consider whether to strengthen their backline in January.

The Catalan club have been dealing with a series of defensive injuries involving Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart. However, Barcelona have not made a final decision on whether to bring in another defender, with the club waiting to assess the injured players’ recoveries.

Sources indicate that laporta’s admiration for Porro reportedly grew during Spain’s World Cup campaign. The Tottenham defender became an crucial part of the national team, developing a strong understanding with Lamine Yamal on the right flank and scoring twice during the tournament, including in the semi-final against France.

Laporta watched that semi-final in Dallas and was reportedly impressed by Porro’s performance. Barcelona had also gathered information about the defender towards the end of the previous summer transfer window, but their enquiry did not progress into a formal proposal to either the player or Tottenham.

Sources indicate that porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a strong negotiating position. The 27-year-old renewed his contract shortly before the World Cup, committing his future to the north London club until 2031.

According to recent reports, reports have also indicated that Tottenham would demand a significant fee to consider allowing the defender to leave. Real Madrid have also been linked with an interest in the Spain international, potentially creating further competition for his signature.

Barcelona’s admiration for Porro is a reminder of the defender’s standing in European football, but there is at the moment no confirmed bid or formal approach.

Tottenham will be keen to retain a player who remains an vital part of their plans. His long-term contract also means the club are under no immediate pressure to negotiate a sale.

The situation could develop if Barcelona decide their defensive injury problems require January reinforcements. For now, however, Spurs remain in a strong position, and any interested club would likely have to make a substantial offer to test their resolve.

  • If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.
  • France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

According to recent reports, as a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.

The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

Sources indicate that "This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he mentioned.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

"French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.

For more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.

Recent findings suggest that france last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how promptly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

In a recent development, the main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

The higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that these figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is presently estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.

According to recent reports, the trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

"For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

In a recent development, RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire.".

"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales.".

Their common message, he said, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts.".

Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.

"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

According to recent reports, "In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier remarked.

This article was originally written in German.

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne stated. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal.

According to recent reports, ‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’.

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

Industry observers note that ‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most crucial thing.’.

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a fresh contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

In a recent development, all eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

According to recent reports, ‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’.

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

According to recent reports, maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca noted.

‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’.

Gustavo Varela is an interesting transfer for Liverpool to explore.

His age coupled with his keen eye for goal are two major boxes that Liverpool like to tick when looking for attackers and, if the fee that Monza want is reasonable, there's no reason why a deal couldn't be explored.

Vinko Marinovic's side may at the moment occupy a qualification playoff spot in 21st, but they will target further progress heading into Thursday's encounter with Atalanta.

While Atalanta should pose the greatest threat yet to Krajiski Ponos' European home winning streak, the hosts enter this week's matchday-four encounter buoyed by three consecutive victories.

The Bergamaschi may be favourites, but Sarri's men remain unconvincing despite their three-match unbeaten run.

November has certainly been eventful in Bergamo, where La Dea entered a training retreat after a humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Parma before drawing 1-1 with Kairat on matchday three to begin their current unbeaten sequence.

That draw was followed by a 1-0 victory over Monza and a thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter Milan at the weekend, when Sarri's men recovered from deficits of 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2 to snatch a point against the defending league champions.

Although they have claimed only one victory during their current unbeaten run, it represents La Dea's longest such sequence since the opening four matches of the campaign, when they recorded three wins, and they will hope to build on that progress in Banja Luka on Thursday.

Victory could lift them into the coveted top eight, although the cluster of clubs on seven points, stretching from fifth-placed Brighton & Hove Albion to 10th-placed St Truidense, means little is guaranteed for an Atalanta side presently on four as the league phase enters a crucial period.

Industry observers note that arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report claims an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

Sources indicate that january looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside states Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

Sources indicate that TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

According to recent reports, the role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

In a recent development, no, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

According to recent reports, the only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met.
  • Industry observers note that the numbers explain the concern.
  • Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

Industry observers note that the numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

In a recent development, A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, says Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two new studies. “This is a really big deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The firm also launched their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has declared plans to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

It has been revealed that but when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

Amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she said: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

Neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

Recent findings suggest that artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most vital value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

Do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, indicates public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

It has been revealed that in the second episode of Nature Podcast’s climate miniseries, host Nick Petrić Howe hears from scientists about what humanity can actually do to stop the runaway train of rising temperatures. The rise of renewable-energy technologies is already making a dent in greenhouse-gas emissions, experts say. But creating meat alternatives and a move away from an economic system that incentivizes ‘growth at any cost’ could help to really shift the dial.

Nature Podcast | 45 min listen or read the transcript.

Vertebrate palaeontologist Aldo Benites-Palomino explains why the extinct ancient whale — which evolved extreme facial asymmetry to to make space in its head for echolocation and sound production organs — was named with a Peruvian word for “anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically”. (Discover | 7 min read).

Reference: Communications Biology paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03797-3.

Researchers have found that the plants’ unusual method of photosynthesis can be harnessed to generate a small amount of electricity, with around eight prickly pears together generating nearly three times the voltage of a standard AA battery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

It has been revealed that his form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

Recent findings suggest that fotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

In a recent development, the timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Industry observers note that iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 15:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 15:10.

Seeking to extend their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League, Juventus will welcome Omonia to Turin on Thursday evening.

While Juve are on track for automatic qualification to the last 16, their visitors are bound for the knockout playoffs as things stand.

More accustomed to Champions League football, Juventus have made a strong start to their campaign in Europe's second tier, claiming 10 points from a possible 12 so far.

After a 5-0 cruise at home to NEC, the Italian giants secured victory over Celta Vigo on matchday two, before playing out a 2-2 draw against Rennes.

Last time out, they retained a top-eight spot by beating AZ in Alkmaar, where Teun Koopmeiners scored against his former club in a tense 2-1 win.

Since then, results have somewhat improved in Serie A, after Juve had made an inconsistent start; four points from two games have lifted Luciano Spalletti's side up to sixth place.

Having fought back twice to salvage a draw with Fiorentina, they then put four goals past lowly Venezia, inspired by Nick Woltemade's half-time introduction from the bench.

However, Spalletti's injury-hit squad still trail 11 points behind league leaders Lazio, while Italy's tight top-four fight could go all the way.

Before facing fellow contenders Como on Sunday, Juve will aim to maintain their undefeated home record in the Europa League, having won six games and drawn nine in Turin since the competition began.

Juventus have also won all four prior meetings with Omonia Nicosia, beating them over two legs in both the 1977-78 European Cup and the 1999-00 UEFA Cup - the Cypriot side lost 10-2 on the latter occasion.

While Juve sit fifth in the Europa League table on 10 points, Omonia's tally of six leaves them 18th midway through the league phase, so defeat could see them drop into the elimination zone.

After coming through qualifying, then winning two of their first three games, Henning Berg's side suffered a 3-1 defeat to NEC on matchday four, despite seizing the lead through Lois Diony's opening goal.

Industry observers note that since that setback, they have beaten Anorthosis Famagusta and drawn 1-1 with city rivals APOEL, with Diony scoring on both occasions. As a result, the Nicosia club are fifth in the Cypriot top flight, five points shy of the summit.

Their domestic title defence may not be going to initiative, but Omonia are on track to escape a Europa League group or league phase for the first time to date - albeit potentially via the playoffs.

Juventus form (all competitions):.

Juventus still have a long absence list, and Kerim Alajbegovic is set to join it on Thursday evening, after picking up a minor thigh problem against Venezia.

Pierre Kalulu and Nico Gonzalez are expected to return from injury this weekend, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Kamil Grabara and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined.

Newcastle United loanee Woltemade now has nine goal contributions for the Bianconeri, having either scored or assisted in all four Europa League appearances.

Likely to support Randal Kolo Muani up front, the German striker also ranks second for shots attempted and for open-play chances created in this season's league phase.

Meanwhile, French forward Diony should lead Omonia's attack, after scoring in three consecutive matches.

Though Hungary international Loic Nego recently returned from a layoff, Carel Eiting is still ruled out by a long-term knee injury.

Juventus possible starting lineup:.

Vicario; Celik, Gatti, Bremer, Cabal; Sarr, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, Woltemade, Boga; Kolo Muani.

Omonia possible starting lineup:.

Kaminski; Mayambela, Coulibaly, Satka, Duverne; Andreou, Maric; Ewandro, Tanase, Montnor; Diony.

Both sides have scored in every league-phase game, and the evidence suggests that trend should continue.

Juventus may be fallen giants but they are still too strong for most opponents at this level - and particularly when playing on home turf.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A government spokesman has stated that, despite talks with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB), the International Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) and others, the impasse caused by last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling remains.

Sources indicate that since the October 30 decision, several leading ice hockey nations — including Finland, Sweden and Czechia — have mentioned they would refrain from playing against Russia in any tournament in which it is allowed to take part. Several key sponsors have also threatened to pull out, should the Russians be allowed to play.

The first tournament to be affected would be the Men's World Juniors, which opens in Canada in late December, followed by the IIHF's premier event, the Men's World Ice Championship, to be hosted by Germany in May.

Stefan Kornelius, the spokesman for Germany's government, told reporters in Berlin on Friday that talks held with various stakeholders had made clear that Russia's participation would render the hosting of the championship "practically impossible — both from a sporting and an economic perspective.".

Kornelius mentioned talks would continue and the government still hoped for a diplomatic solution that would allow Germany to host the championship — as planned — in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf in May.

According to recent reports, "Our goal must be to hold the tournaments as scheduled," he said. "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore — through dialogue — how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Following the CAS ruling that the IIHF must allow Russia to return to international play, DEB chairman Frank Lutz had conceded that Germany may be forced to consider withdrawing as championship host.

Asked at Friday's press conference whether Germany could issue visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman declined to answer categorically, but did indicate that this would be difficult under restrictions at the moment in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," mentioned spokesperson Martin Giese.

Earlier this week, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney categorically ruled out Russian players taking part in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he said.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors," he stated, "the Russians will not be there.".

Russian President Vladimir Putin has also weighed in on the glitch, accusing countries opposing Russia's return to international sport of violating the rights of his country's athletes.

Sources indicate that the IIHF Council had originally called two days of meetings, on Monday and Tuesday, to try to reach a consensus on how to respond to the CAS decision — before extending discussions for a third day, on Thursday. By Friday, its members had evidently still not reached a consensus.

This comes as the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship, which is not affected by the CAS decision, opened in Denmark — and with the clock ticking toward the start of the World Juniors in Alberta on December 26.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal like Kevin Schade, but he isn’t the winger they want most.
  • Sources indicate that the ranking reflects an awkward summer for Mikel Arteta.
  • Tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal like Kevin Schade, but he isn’t the winger they want most. Football.London’s Tom Canton reports that the Brentford forward is on the shortlist for the left flank, with RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa ranked above him. Canton states the 24-year-old Germany international is certainly appreciated at the Emirates.

Sources indicate that the ranking reflects an awkward summer for Mikel Arteta. Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Vinicius Junior and signed only Christos Tzolis for about £34m.

Tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have covered since, and Madueke rescued a point in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, which left Arsenal six points clear for now.

Nusa, the 21-year-old Norwegian winger, has six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig. Sky Sports reports that the Bundesliga club won’t sell him in January, so a summer deal looks more realistic, with Leipzig reportedly valuing him between £60m and £77m. Schade is the quicker route, but Arsenal asked about him in the summer and got nowhere, according to TEAMtalk. His contract runs until 2028.

Schade has scored three times in ten Premier League appearances from 2.44 expected goals, and his pace suits a side that already creates through Tzolis. He can play either flank or centrally. The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Industry observers note that not in January, and certainly not as a consolation. Arsenal lead the league, Tzolis remains the first-choice left winger, and Madueke has just shown he can deliver there. Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

Nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

  • Industry observers note that part of the money is already committed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

According to recent reports, juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Industry observers note that part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its latest authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

Industry observers note that the squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

In a recent development, the assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

Recent findings suggest that for supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

In a recent development, shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

Recent findings suggest that the terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

  • Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 16:43.

Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis.

Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.

Milan will head into the second half of the league phase with a point to prove, having lost three out of four games to date - including the last two without scoring.

Recently beaten by Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, Ruben Amorim's side have failed to even find the scoresheet since Goncalo Ramos struck in their lone win against Red Bull Salzburg.

A paltry tally of three points leaves the Italian heavyweights in real danger of being knocked out, as they sit 28th in the Europa League table and only the top 24 will go through.

By contrast with their continental results, Milan are showing clear signs of progress in Serie A, where they occupy fourth place, just ahead of city rivals and reigning champions Inter.

The Rossoneri have taken 15 points from the last available 18 - while scoring at least twice on each occasion - and they have only lost one domestic fixture this term.

Aiming to keep pace in the Scudetto race, Amorim's men hosted surprise high-flyers Frosinone last weekend, when they eventually cruised to a 5-1 win, with rising star Alphadjo Cisse scoring again.

However, Milan must now head to Greece, where they memorably won the 1994 Champions League final but have never beaten native hosts in six prior attempts.

In particular, Milan's two previous visits to Piraeus ended with a 2-2 draw in 1959 and a 3-1 defeat in 2018, when Olympiacos won the most recent meeting.

That was also in the Europa League, and the Greek giants at the moment sit sixth in this season's league phase - seven points clear of the Rossoneri.

As things stand, Olympiacos will directly enter the last 16, despite losing their perfect record last time out.

Across all competitions, they had won nine straight games before being held to a 0-0 draw by Rennes, which followed victories over Jagiellonia Bialystok, Marseille and Sparta Prague.

All told, Imanol Alguacil's side have lost just one of their last 18 fixtures, and Sunday's 6-2 destruction of 10-man Iraklis left them second in the Greek Superleague standings.

Furthermore, Olympiacos have only suffered one defeat in their last 13 Europa League matches - while keeping nine clean sheets - so they will surely fear no-one on home turf.

Olympiacos form (all competitions):.

AC Milan form (all competitions):.

Amorim has typically shuffled his lineup for Europa League games - albeit not to positive effect - and several fringe players should feature for Milan.

Omari Hutchinson and Ardon Jashari have often played, while Cisse could start again; the latest Italy international already has six Serie A goals and he scored a hat-trick away to Salzburg earlier in the campaign.

At the other end of the spectrum, experienced captain Mike Maignan can return after serving a one-match ban for his red card against Bournemouth.

Goncalo Ramos is set to overcome a minor calf problem, but the visitors must travel without Mattia Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek due to injury.

Meanwhile, Olympiacos are missing long-term absentees Ayoub El-Kaabi and Yusuf Yazici, plus South American pair Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze.

Leon Bailey bagged two goals and an assist at the weekend, so he could link up with Armando Gonzalez, who is the hosts' top Europa League scorer with two.

Portuguese playmaker Jota Silva has racked up the most shots in this season's league phase; however, just two of those 17 attempts have found the target and none have hit the net.

Olympiacos possible starting lineup:.

Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

AC Milan possible starting lineup:.

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Rabiot, Cisse; Ramos.

Milan may have struggled to score in Europe, but with Amorim developing an exciting front line, they average above two goals per game in Serie A and are overdue to convert some chances.

That said, Olympiacos are a formidable force on home soil, so they can keep their unbeaten streak going with a hard-fought draw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet indicates Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Sources indicate that barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and says he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Recent findings suggest that palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and noted needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, according to fussball-news.de, which names them and Arsenal as the most interested clubs.

Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old. Liverpool and Milan are reportedly preparing concrete steps for the winter window, although the report attributes no bid to either.

Dortmund will not make it easy. They want to keep a player contracted until June 2029 and strategy to raise his salary, while Svensson feels settled and has no wish for a rushed move. A sale would cost at least €45m (about £38m), and Premier League clubs are ready to test Dortmund with a €30m (roughly £25m) offer, yet FotMob values him at just €23m.

The numbers explain the interest. Svensson has started all 10 Bundesliga games this season. His expected assists total of 1.13 comes without a single assist, and he has made 22 tackles, 14 interceptions and 45 recoveries while passing at 86.1%. He can play in midfield.

The flaws are clear. He has won only eight of 29 aerial duels and landed six of 32 crosses. He also plays as a wing-back in front of a back three, so Andoni Iraola’s back four would ask him to defend more of the flank alone.

In a recent development, iraola’s 4-2-3-1 sends full-backs forward, and Milos Kerkez, bought for a reported £40m last year, has no goals or assists in the Premier League this season. Kostas Tsimikas, 30, is the backup on a contract that expires next year.

Not in January, and not at €45m. A €30m offer would fail, and £38m for a player FotMob values at €23m is poor business. Summer 2027 is the realistic window, once Tsimikas’s deal has run down.

The bigger problem sits on the other flank. Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back while injuries have hit that position all season, so Iraola needs a natural right-back more urgently than a second left-back. Kerkez is 22 and signed until 2030, so Svensson would challenge him rather than replace him, which is healthy given Kerkez’s lack of end product.

Kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

Latest Update: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond massive promises?

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.
  • Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".
  • From November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.

Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".

From November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis. Turkey is the official host, and Australia will lead the negotiations. But the issues they'll confront during those 12 days are far more serious than the showy marketing campaign make them out to be.

Severe drought, extreme heat, wildfires and record-low water levels in Europe's main waterways — summer across the continent was dominated by climate emergencies.

And in late August, a series of flash floods triggered by a rock-ice avalanche in Nepal and Tibet washed away entire villages, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands missing. Climate experts have linked the disaster to melting ice and a warming climate.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Globally, carbon emissions are still rising: the UN has concluded that it is no longer possible to keep global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels, the goal agreed at COP21 in 2015.

Sources indicate that the global transition away from polluting fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas will be at the center of attention in Antalya — once again. To date, there's been no consensus on whether and how to transition rapidly away from this main source of global warming.

Despite the setbacks, the world has made some progress thanks to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

David Victor, a climate expert at the University of California San Diego, pointed out that before then, the planet was hurtling toward an average temperature rise of between 3-3.5 C.

If current climate commitments are fully implemented, the latest UN projections show a rise of up to 2.6 C. It's a significant step forward, even though warming of that magnitude will still have worldwide consequences.

"There's no question that we could be doing more," stated Victor, though he cautioned against pinning too much on this year's summit.

All agreements at COP need to be unanimous, meaning individual states can quash any sweeping resolutions. Added to that challenge are the ongoing wars, trade conflicts and other economic problems swirling around this year's negotiations.

Industry observers note that "It's like a giant Christmas tree in which everybody's hung their different ornaments, and the tree is groaning and more ornaments are being put on it," stated Victor. "We have to look at it for what it is: It's a place where people talk about stuff.".

Instead of waiting for all COP member states to agree, Victor sees a better chance for change in what he called "clubs" — smaller alliances of governments and companies working together to advance actual solutions, whether it be in aviation, shipping or electromobility.

Recent findings suggest that "The Paris process is key. It has to go forward," he told DW. "But all the work is going to be done in clubs.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An example of this approach was last April's first ever International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia.

Colombia and the Netherlands invited representatives from 57 countries and key sectors to discuss ways to move the world away from coal, oil and gas, after an agreement on a similar plan failed at the 2025 climate summit due to opposition from several oil-producing states.

It has been revealed that with an eye to the ongoing trade conflicts and energy crisis, hosts Turkey and Australia have included green industrialization and the clean energy transition among their aims. One goal is to increase the share of electricity in global energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 20% today.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A recent analysis by the International Energy Agency found accelerating electrification could cut fuel-importing countries' energy bills by more than $400 billion (€357 billion) by 2035, compared to 2025 levels. The idea could appeal to regions dependent on fossil fuel imports — among them Germany and the European Union.

Ahead of COP31, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider mentioned Germany and the EU wanted to spark fresh momentum in the "global phaseout of fossil fuels.".

It's wouldn't just be good for the climate, but a chance for many countries to boost their economies and reduce dependence on energy imports, added Schneider in a statement.

Oil-producing states like Saudi Arabia, however, aren't interested in deals that will undermine their business model. At recent UN climate conferences, they've repeatedly blocked any final agreements, including phaseout aims.

Recent findings suggest that even China, despite its massive expansion of wind and solar energy over the last 20 years, could be against the idea. The economic superpower traditionally rejects any outside demands, proposals or interference concerning its national decisions on energy policy.

Every country in the world is affected by climate change, with loss and damage calculated in the hundreds of billions from heat, drought and storms. Worst hit are vulnerable countries in the Global South and island nations, who are at risk of disappearing as sea levels rise.

In a recent development, that's where money comes into play, with developing countries calling for more support to protect their citizens from the harms of global warming. At the 2024 UN climate talks in Baku, Azerbaijan, industrialized nations agreed to free up at least $300 billion annually in climate financing by 2035.

But where exactly all those funds will come from remains hotly debated. At the same time, several major developed countries — most notably, the US — have cut their development aid.

The German government only paid out €4.7 billion from its 2025 budget for international climate financing, down from €6.1 billion in 2024.

"The level of financial support for developing countries today is far from what's needed," said Jan Kowalzig, a climate expert at Oxfam Germany.

Breaking financial promises like this comes at the expense of losing the trust of developing countries and, as a result, the diplomatic power which Germany and other industrialized nations rely on to shape policy to fight climate change.

Cosima Cassel, who focuses on climate diplomacy at the independent think tank E3G in Berlin, believes Turkey's push to turbocharge electrification during an oil crisis could be successful.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For Cassel, a successful outcome at what are expected to be difficult negotiations in Antalya would reveal actual political will behind the grand agreements.

When it comes to electrification, that means taking the expansion of electricity grids and battery storage capacity seriously — not to mention removing the barriers to further electrification.

This article was originally written in German.

It has been revealed that pochettino inherits a club in trouble: one win and eight points from ten league games, 18th place and Michael Carrick’s sacking after their worst league start in 40 years. Recent findings suggest that mcKennie, 28, offers versatility: Spalletti has used him on both wings, at wing-back and even as a striker, and he managed eight goals and five assists in 38 appearances before signing his upcoming deal in March. This season the output has dipped, with FotMob showing one goal, no assists and a 6.98 rating from eight Serie A starts. His contract runs to 2030, and FotMob values him at about £28m.

Not as a January priority. United’s problem is a team that loses control of matches, and McKennie is a runner who arrives in the box rather than a midfielder who dictates tempo. Put him next to a struggling back four and his versatility becomes a drawback, because Spalletti gets the best from him higher up the pitch, where his goals come from.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

According to recent reports, romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.
